title: Unattended auto-mode reject applies + emails but never seals a tamper-evident decision record
expected: Every solely-automated significant decision (GDPR Art. 22 / EU AI Act) is sealed into the tamper-evident hash-chained System of Record the DecisionRecordsPanel verifies and exports.
got: In rejectMode:'auto' the pass calls actOnPipelineEntry(...,'reject',...,{actor:'system'}) and dispatches the rejection email, writing only the mutable 'auto_rejected' automation event. It never calls sealDecisionSafe — only the supervised screen-wave path seals (screen-wave.ts:215). The least-supervised reject path has the weakest audit integrity.
l2_priority: Seed an auto-mode reject; confirm it is ABSENT from /api/decisions/records (the tamper-evident chain) and present only in the mutable DecisionLog.
suggested_acceptance: Call sealDecisionSafe({kind:'auto_rejected', actor:'auto:policy-pass', policyVersion, candidateRef, rationale, inputs}) on the auto-mode reject apply branch so the hash chain covers every solely-automated reject, not just screen-wave.

title: Candidate disclosure promises per-decision human review that rejectMode:'auto' contradicts
expected: The AI-use disclosure shown to candidates is a truthful representation of how decisions are actually made under every shipped configuration.
got: The disclosure states 'Každé rozhodnutí ... přezkoumává a činí člověk; nic nepříznivého se nerozhoduje automaticky' (every decision is reviewed and made by a human; nothing adverse is decided automatically). True under the 'approve' default and the interactive wave, but FALSE under rejectMode:'auto', where a reject is applied + emailed with no human in the loop.
l2_priority: Confirm which rejectMode ships as the tenant default in a production-like config and whether the auto toggle is reachable to operators.
suggested_acceptance: Either disable rejectMode:'auto' for production tenants, or qualify the disclosure sentence so it cannot be contradicted by a config toggle.

title: Persisted screen-wave audit rationale is English-only in the exported record
expected: A Czech regulator reading the raw exported decision record sees a rationale in cs.
got: The persisted rationale string is byte-stable English by design (screen-wave.ts:22-23,174); cs is rendered UI-side from reasonCode/reasonParams (ScreenWaveModal.tsx:122-132). The decision-records.json export therefore carries English rationales.
suggested_acceptance: Include the structured reasonCode/reasonParams in the sealed record so an export can render a localized rationale alongside the stable English string.

title: STRENGTH — fairness shielding fails closed (early-career + unknown archetype shielded, drift recorded)
expected: A protected-class / unclassifiable candidate is never auto-rejected by data drift.
got: isFairnessProtected shields early-career AND any unknown/renamed archetype from auto-reject; an unrecognized archetype is recorded as fairness_gate_unknown_archetype rather than silently rejected, and the automation pass re-asserts the invariant as defense-in-depth.
suggested_acceptance: Protect this fail-closed behavior; pin it with the existing tests.

title: STRENGTH — interactive wave previews before it mutates; explicit human commit gates every reject
expected: No solely-automated rejection: a human can see who would be rejected and must explicitly authorize.
got: ScreenWaveModal dry-runs on open + every slider change with per-row rationales; only an explicit 'Reject and notify' commit (dryRun:false) mutates. The scheduled pass defaults rejectMode to 'approve', queuing rejects for a human click.

title: STRENGTH — tamper-evident hash-chained decision record, verified + exportable
expected: A regulator-handable record: input, actor, reason, timestamp, policy version, with integrity proof.
got: sealDecisionRecord links each row via content_hash; verifyDecisionChain recomputes the chain to detect any after-the-fact edit; DecisionRecordsPanel leads with the verify badge and exports the whole chain in one click for a right-to-explanation request.
suggested_acceptance: Protect the System of Record; extend its coverage per lucie-screening-01.

title: STRENGTH — AI-use disclosure + GDPR consent shown before submission, in plain Czech
expected: Candidate sees a plain-language AI disclosure + consent before AI processing; not pre-ticked, not buried.
got: AiDisclosure with showDataConsent renders on the conversational apply (ConversationalApply.tsx:601) and quick-apply (QuickApplyForm.tsx:126) surfaces; copy is plain cs with a 12-month retention statement, human-review right, and a self-service erasure link; consent is recorded server-side at submit (apply route recordEntryConsent) with an append-only audit trail.
l2_priority: Confirm the disclosure is visible BEFORE submit on the live apply page (token fixture) and the consent event lands in the candidate drawer.
suggested_acceptance: Keep the disclosure-before-submit pattern; reconcile its copy with rejectMode per lucie-screening-02.

title: Fairness matrix degrades to 'uniform / adds nothing' when weights weren't adjusted — can read as 'no fairness check ran'
expected: An auditor can tell a PASSED fairness check (cross-scheme tested, order robust) from an ABSENT one.
got: When no candidate's weighting diverged, FairnessPanel shows 'fairnessUniform' instead of the matrix — correct and honest, but to an auditor it can read as the check not having run rather than having passed.
l2_priority: Confirm copy framing live; verify the matrix renders with real per-candidate divergence when weights DO adjust.
suggested_acceptance: Reframe the uniform-state copy as a passed check ('cross-scheme tested; weights converged, order robust') rather than an absence.

title: STRENGTH — AI vs rule-based source disclosed on every group-eval output
expected: Every headline AI output discloses its provenance; no non-disclosed AI verdict acts on a candidate.
got: AiVerdict carries an explicit aiBacked/rule-based pill; FairnessPanel discloses llm-tuned vs rule-based weights.
l2_priority: Confirm the live pill reflects the actual generation path (AI vs deterministic fallback).
suggested_acceptance: Keep the source-disclosure pills on every AI surface.

title: STRENGTH — fairness is reasoned, not black-box (real cross-scheme matrix + divergence flag)
expected: The fairness view explains WHY one candidate outranks another.
got: FairnessPanel renders a real cross-scheme matrix (each candidate re-scored under every candidate's bounded weighting), a mean, a robust order, per-candidate weight notes, and flags when the robust order diverges from the headline order.
l2_priority: Confirm cells differ per candidate live (not identical) and the divergence note fires correctly.
suggested_acceptance: Protect the cross-scheme matrix as the legibility primitive.

title: STRENGTH — knockout integrity: a must-have-failing candidate cannot be crowned lead, and the lead is sealed only when KO passes
expected: The recommended lead actually passes the role's must-haves.
got: The ko-aware sort guarantees a must-have-failing candidate can't lead; the lead is sealed to the decision record only when KO passes (group-eval-run.ts:351,402 per the journey grounding map).
l2_priority: Open group-eval-run.ts directly at L2 to confirm the line numbers and the seal-on-KO-pass condition.

title: Audit trail is split across two stores with different integrity guarantees; the tamper-evident one omits autonomous rejects
expected: The strong-integrity (tamper-evident) audit store covers EVERY solely-automated significant decision an auditor would inspect.
got: Lucie's audit surface is two siblings: the mutable DecisionLog (every kind, including auto-mode auto_rejected) and the tamper-evident DecisionRecordsPanel (today only screen-wave seals). The complete picture of autonomous rejections lives in the MUTABLE log; the tamper-evident store is a subset. Same root cause as lucie-screening-01, recorded here because this is the surface where the asymmetry is visible.
l2_priority: With seeded auto-mode rejects, confirm whether they appear in /api/decisions/records (chain) or only in the DecisionLog.
suggested_acceptance: Seal every solely-automated reject into the hash chain so the tamper-evident System of Record matches the DecisionLog's autonomous-reject coverage.

title: STRENGTH — calibration is MEASURED from real outcome pairs with an honest 'not yet calibrated' gate
expected: Confidence scores are calibrated against measured outcomes, not asserted; under-data honestly says so.
got: computeCalibration bins real (score, advance/pass) pairs into a reliability curve + Brier score over every tenant-scoped saved-analysis row; below MIN_CALIBRATION_OUTCOMES (20) the panel refuses to draw a curve and states how many more outcomes are needed. No hardcoded confidence in the path.
l2_priority: Seed outcomes; confirm the curve renders from real pairs and the gate is honest under low data.
suggested_acceptance: Protect the measured-not-asserted calibration + the under-data honesty gate.

title: STRENGTH — decision-log attribution is three-state; an unmapped kind never defaults accountability to the machine
expected: Auto vs human is never silently misattributed in an auditable log.
got: decisionAttribution returns auto|human|unknown; an unmapped kind renders UNKNOWN (not AUTO) and warns in dev, on purpose — defaulting to AUTO would misattribute accountability to the machine. The log is auto/human filterable and CSV-exportable.
suggested_acceptance: Keep the three-state attribution + the never-default-to-auto rule.

title: STRENGTH — decision records exportable with a global chain-integrity verdict
expected: An exportable/inspectable audit trail exists across the AI touch-points.
got: /api/decisions/records returns records + a global verifyDecisionChain verdict; ?candidate scopes to one subject's right-to-explanation dossier; the panel exports the whole chain in one click.
suggested_acceptance: Keep the per-candidate scoped export + global chain verdict.
